chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from Fadala from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Prayer is disliked in three places along the road: Al-Bayda', which is Dhat al-Jaysh and Dhat al-Sasal, and Dajnan. And he said: 'There is no harm in praying between the raised edges (Zawahir), which are the Jawadd, the raised edges of the roads, but it is disliked to pray inside the Jawadd.'

key_terms.الْجَوَادُّ: The sunken/middle part of the road

ai.seo_question: Where is it disliked to pray on the road according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq) to clarify the juristic distinction between praying on the raised edges of the road (al-zawahir), which is permissible, versus the sunken middle (al-jawadd), which is disliked. The hadith specifically identifies three notorious locations—Al-Bayda’ (Dhat al-Jaysh), Dhat al-Sasalil, and Dajnan—as places of particular dislike, likely due to their historical association with battles or specific topographical hazards. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on avoiding places of potential danger or distraction while maintaining the validity of the prayer.
